reason: The cited evidence supports the general concept of using ML surrogates for yield strength prediction and notes their dependence on data/features, but it does not provide any evidence for the specific claims about in situ synchrotron/DIC data integration, physics-informed constraints, or the 50% computation time reduction for HfNbTiVAl10.
premises: A surrogate ML model can predict yield strength faster than physics-based calculations, with some accuracy trade-off.
Surrogate model accuracy depends on dataset, features, and algorithm.
In situ synchrotron diffraction and DIC can capture evolving local strain fields and microstructural dynamics.
Real-time local strain data reflecting heterogeneous microstructure can train a physics-informed ML model to map microstructural descriptors to macroscopic mechanical responses.
Integrating such data into a physics-informed ML surrogate will reduce computation time by ~50% over conventional simulations.
